rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord may only evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance for one of 17 specified just causes, which must be the dominant motive for the eviction. Mere expiration of a rental agreement or change in ownership does not constitute just cause.
rules.quotedSpan: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
rules.coverageDescription: All residential rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.
exemptions: Tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, are exempt from rent increase limitations but remain subject to just-cause eviction requirements.
Tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act are exempt from rent increase limitations but remain subject to just-cause eviction requirements.
Tenancies where rent is regulated by another government agency are exempt from rent increase limitations but remain subject to just-cause eviction requirements.
warnings: The source does not provide an effective date for when this requirement began; the web page is informational and does not cite the original ordinance enactment date.
